name: Noadiah
overview: Noadiah was a male Levite mentioned in the book of Ezra. He is uniquely identified as a Levite who was present at the counting of the silver, gold, and utensils, indicating his role in the religious and administrative duties of the post-exilic community. Scripture does not provide additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Noadiah means 'meet with YHWH,' reflecting a theophoric element that emphasizes a connection with the Lord. This proper name underscores his identity within the covenant community but was not indicated as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Noadiah is recorded as the father of Binnui, establishing a direct familial relationship. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Noadiah's significance lies in his participation as a Levite in the careful accounting of sacred resources during the restoration period under Ezra. His involvement highlights the Levites' vital role in maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple service after the exile. This underscores the faithful stewardship required in the community's renewed worship and covenantal life.
